source_type_decision.reason: The restored source asks for a concrete Go concurrency implementation using two goroutines to alternately print 1 through 100; the expected artifact is executable synchronization code plus ordering/deadlock/race reasoning.

verified_claims: The source asks: 使用两个协程（Goroutines）交替打印 1-100.
The source context is a Go/PHP backend interview, so a Go implementation is the correct language boundary.

primary_sources_checked.title: The Go Programming Language Specification
verified_claims: A go statement starts a function call as an independently executing goroutine.
Channels created with make support send and receive; a channel may be used by multiple goroutines for communication.
A channel with capacity one can hold the single initial turn token without requiring a simultaneous receiver.

primary_sources_checked.title: The Go Memory Model
verified_claims: A send on a channel is synchronized before completion of its corresponding receive, which supports the candidate's cross-goroutine ordering argument.
Programs with shared mutable data should serialize access using channels or other synchronization primitives.

primary_sources_checked.title: sync package documentation
verified_claims: WaitGroup.Wait blocks until the task counter reaches zero.
Positive Add calls that start from a zero counter should occur before Wait and are typically issued before starting the goroutine being waited for.
WaitGroup.Go was added in Go 1.25, so Add/Done remains the more backward-compatible interview form.

primary_sources_checked.title: Deterministic Go race/order validation
verified_claims: The exact implementation and test bytes pass go test -race under Go 1.23.2 in an isolated module.
The test repeats the exercise 100 times and checks every output position is exactly 1 through 100.
No race is reported and no run deadlocks.

findings.finding: The candidate answers the source in Go rather than reusing the repository's old Java placeholder, preserving the language-specific Goroutine/channel boundary.
The two turn channels encode a single-token invariant, so each output is preceded by an explicit handoff instead of relying on scheduler timing or sleep.
The terminal condition is correct: after printing 100, the even worker does not send another odd token, avoiding the classic final-send deadlock.
WaitGroup is correctly separated from ordering: Add/Done/Wait control completion while channel communication controls turn order.
The reproducible test checks exact sequence across 100 runs and enables the Go race detector; this materially exceeds one-shot visual output checking.
